correctness.rationale: Exact finite incidence sieve of all 59048 nonzero ternary cubics gives 7488 rationally nonsingular tangent-filling forms, verified coefficient-by-coefficient by independent C++ and NumPy implementations. Scalar normalization leaves 3744 forms; full GL3(F3) generators produce exactly three disjoint projective orbits of sizes 936, 936 and 1872. Algebraic-closure smoothness of each orbit representative is proven by gradient equations, not bounded extension tests. The minimum-degree argument excludes every irreducible conic and line.

originality.rationale: The primary 2023 tangent-filling paper defines the property and poses its general minimum-degree problem but does not compute the smooth cubic locus over F3 or classify rational tangent configurations there. The 2022 blocking-curve paper is about the different incidence condition that original rational curve points meet every line, whereas each of these three representatives is nonblocking and its dual tangent set is blocking. Exact orbit enumeration and the degree-three minimum answer are not direct consequences of either published statement. The overlap searches uncovered no equivalent published theorem, while residual unindexed elliptic-curve table priority is acknowledged.
residual_risks: A historical enumeration of all cubic or elliptic-plane projective isomorphism classes over F3 might implicitly encode this subset and could support a publication-priority claim after additional comparison.
An unindexed finite-geometric study of six-point dual blocking arrangements arising as tangent images might supply equivalent orbit information.
No independent external mathematical audit or publication-priority certification was performed.

value.rationale: The minimum irreducible tangent-filling degree over F3 answers the q=3 case of Asgarli–Ghioca Question 1.5. The theorem also exhausts the natural smooth minimum-degree arithmetic locus, distinguishes three dual tangent-line blocking geometries, supplies explicit reps and exact projective stabilizers, and shows that the tangent-filling curves need not be primal blocking. These are motivated by a stated mathematical question and are not arbitrary point-count slices.
